chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no objection to withdrawal (al-'azl) from a free woman if her husband desires it, and if she dislikes it, she has no authority (to prevent it) in the matter."

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ الْحُرَّةِ: The free woman (as opposed to a slave)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on coitus interruptus (azl) and does the wife's consent matter?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the legal ruling of 'azl' (coitus interruptus) in Islamic jurisprudence, clarifying that the husband has the sole discretion to perform withdrawal during intercourse, and the wife's consent or dissent does not legally invalidate the act. In Shia fiqh, this is often discussed under the principle of 'tamlik al-manafi'' (ownership of benefits), where the husband retains the right to derive sexual pleasure without the wife's veto, provided it does not cause harm. This ruling highlights the asymmetry in marital rights regarding procreation versus pleasure in classical juristic interpretations.
